keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Kaska; its Hittite shapes of -1400 to -1200 draw the same mountains as Hittite land. The page gives no area; it places the Kaska in 'mountainous East Pontic Anatolia' between the core Hittite region and the Black Sea and says they probably came from the eastern shore of the Propontis. The Pontus region (60,000 km2, 34.3-41.3 E, 40.0-42.0 N) is the researcher's reading, deliberately soft: the cities they held (Nerik, Zalpuwa, Kammama, Nenassa) are named but not located on the page.

sources.title: Kaskians
sources.note: First attestation c. 1450 under Hantili II, Tudhaliya II c. 1430, the c. 1330 burning of Hattusa, Mursili II and Pihhuniya, the early 13th century sack of Hattusa, Tiglath-Pileser I in the late 12th century; no infobox, no area, no capital.

notes: Cliopatria has no Kaska; the hittites dossier (me-04-a) does not record the Kaska at all (no contest, no loss of Nerik or Hattusa), so the contest events here have no matching entry there and me-04-a's reviewer should decide whether Hittite shapes of -1400..-1200 should draw the Pontic mountains as contested or as outside the empire. The first page tried, Kaska_people, is the Kaska Dena of British Columbia (wrong article); the Hittite-era Kaska are at Kaskians. The Kaska are 'loosely affiliated' tribes with no kingdom, so the state here is a soft Pontus-wide reading; the end (late 12th century, Tiglath-Pileser I) is bridged to -1112. The page's Caucasus (Kolkha/Colchis) and Cappadocia links are unconfirmed and not drawn. Page budget: one page (plus the failed Kaska_people). [Reviewer me-04-x, 2026-10-19: the placeholder capital 'none (tribal union; placeholder in the Pontic mountains)' at 37.8 E 40.9 N was removed: the Kaskians page names no capital ('loosely affiliated' tribes), and the schema keeps the capitals list empty for stateless entities, so the map should not draw a seat that did not exist.]
